title: ‘Worst defence decision ever’? AUKUS inquiry gets China wrong | The Strategist
paragraphs: The key verdict of the public inquiry into AUKUS lacks credibility.

The privately run exercise tells us that AUKUS is ‘the worst, riskiest and most costly defence decision ever made by an Australian government’. But this rests on false strategic premises: that China poses little threat to Australia, that war with China would never be strategically justified, and that the primary threat to Australian sovereignty is the United States.

The unofficial AUKUS Public Inquiry was launched this year to ‘assess the implications of AUKUS for Australia’s long-term peace and security.’ With chairs including former chief of the Australian Defence Force Chris Barrie and former environment minister Peter Garrett, the inquiry was framed as an opportunity to publicly scrutinise the case for AUKUS.
